items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: So I would say Maria is hitting the nail on the head.

ctx.x: Yes certainly. I’m an avid reader so I’m just always looking for – sometimes it’s new information but also I’m an avid reader of novels. Oddly enough I was just thinking about this yesterday. Somebody asked me one of those impossible questions – it’s an impossible, it’s a ridiculous question, but he said, “Would you rather go blind or deaf?” you know that old sort of mental acrobatics to try to imagine yourself into either of those

things which is of course impossible when you have both of those faculties. But it was a real struggle because I thought reading for me is as important as music in some ways, to really lose myself in a world that somebody else has imagined and then is giving to me through the means of the page, where I’m – as I’m reading their world I’m creating my own world. And I think there is something so fundamentally important about that for me that I’m not sure I could be a composer or a musician if I couldn’t experience…
You did the opposite of what Phil Woods had said about young musicians. And his advice was well if you can be a doctor or a tenor player, be the doctor. And you went the other way.
